tech.title: Incident injected: Replayable batch blocks checkout

events.caption: checkout starts failing (4 timed out so far).

tech.title: Checkout degraded: 4 timeouts since injection, success 0%
12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 89908 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 4.1s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
Checkout over last 15s: 43/48 succeeded (90%), 5 timeouts.
Checkout success 82% over 10s (5/28 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $3,286/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

tech.title: R1 proposes wait

detail.rationale: The root blocker (pid 89908) has been idle in transaction for only 4.1s with a trivial last statement (SELECT 1). Checkout is degraded (82% success vs 95% SLO, $3,286/min at risk per BIZ-1) but the business tolerates up to 60s of degradation. Terminating a batch_worker without knowing its replayability, interrupt policy, or whether it holds protected settlements (EVIDENCE CHECKLIST shows biz.workload_registry, db.protected_settlements, biz.change_calendar, and biz.tradeoff are all MISSING) carries unbounded risk. Waiting for the missing probes lets us make an evidence-based decision in the next round.

tech.title: R1 after investigating: switches to terminate:batch_replayable_inventory

detail.rationale: The trade-off analysis (BIZ-5) shows waiting costs ~$114,476 in lost checkout revenue and exceeds the 60s degradation tolerance, while terminating costs only a 4-minute replay of an idempotent, replayable job with policy 'may_interrupt' (BIZ-2). No protected settlements are in flight (DB-2) and no change-calendar window blocks interruption (BIZ-3). The blocker has been idle in transaction for 4.1s (DB-1), indicating it is not actively working.
